context.objective: Document how we carry out Cash Reconciliation & Working Capital Reporting, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?

Three things can start it. Cash activity shows up in the bank portal, or the monthly bank reconciliation turns up activity, or there is a planned capital event that needs a liquidity analysis. We are meant to update the Cash Composition workbook daily whenever cash moves, but honestly that often slips to weekly or monthly, and that is where the trouble starts. The first place it bites is the starting balance. When I carry the workbook into a new period, the beginning balance has to match the prior ending balance and the actual bank balance including the sweep accounts. If it does not, I record the exception and I do not move that item forward until it is resolved or an authorized decision is documented.
When the starting balances do not match, how do you investigate the discrepancy?

For the starting balance itself, I trace it back to the prior ending records, meaning the prior reconciled workbook and the bank records, because the beginning balance has to be traceable to those. I should be honest that there is no confirmed correction procedure for the carry-forward, so I do not know the official way to fix it or who approves the fix. The process owner would have to confirm that. Where I do the real digging is later, when the cash categories do not add up to the bank balance. Then I look for four things: missing transactions, duplicated entries, broken formulas or links, and misclassifications, and I keep going until the categorized total matches the actual bank balance including the sweep accounts. There is no tolerance at all. People sometimes say an item under ten dollars is typical, but that is not an approved rounding tolerance and I cannot use it as one. Any difference that is left gets escalated with a variance note, and nobody should rely on the report until it is resolved and documented.
Once you identify a missing transaction, duplicate, broken formula or misclassification, what do you do to correct it?

It depends which one it is. A missing movement I add as its own row in the Cash Analysis tab with the date, description, amount and cash category, after I have confirmed the account, entity, date, amount and whether the cash came in or went out against the bank record. Duplicates usually happen because the same movement got picked up from the bank portal and then again from the monthly bank reconciliation, so I make sure it sits in the list only once and matches the bank record. Broken links or formulas I correct and document before the workbook is used again. The hard one is misclassification, because often the real problem is that I cannot tell what the cash was for. If I cannot assign a transaction to a category I do not guess. It stays as an explicit exception, I go to the fund team or the client for the transaction details, and that item stops until it is resolved and documented with the supporting documents or correspondence. One more thing: if the fix would change prior-year history, I only change it when there are supporting records and the change has been reviewed.
After you correct a transaction, how is that change checked before the workbook is used again?

Mostly by me, and that is a weakness. On every update I rerun three checks myself: the total of all the cash categories has to equal the bank balance, every category has to trace to identifiable activity, and each movement has to be in the transaction list only once. A reviewer looks at the bank-to-category match, and the reconciliation is the record of that. For the category-support check and the duplicate check, I perform them but who reviews or approves them has never been confirmed, so I cannot tell you who signs those off. The day-to-day copy in the Treasury folder gets a lot less review than the quarterly copy. The proper detailed review only happens quarterly, when the report is copied into the quarterly supporting files and the quarterly reviewer goes through it, and any corrections made in the quarterly copy get listed. If any of the checks fails it is the same rule every time: record the exception and do not advance the affected item until it is resolved or an authorized decision is documented.
What does the quarterly reviewer examine in the detailed review?

I am not the reviewer, so I can only tell you what I see from my side. They review the quarterly copy and the differences that have been identified, and the test is that the quarterly output reconciles to the approved source data for that period. What tends to go wrong there is that the quarterly copy and the Treasury-folder copy do not agree. When that happens we identify the differences and escalate the need to keep the two copies aligned. It goes to the reviewer or the process owner, although the final owner of that has not been confirmed. We only proceed once the versions agree or the difference is approved and documented, and we keep a version comparison and a resolution record. What I cannot tell you is how corrections made in the quarterly copy are supposed to get back into the operational copy. That method has not been confirmed, and neither has who owns keeping the two aligned. The process owner and whoever handles records management would need to confirm it. And if someone already relied on an earlier report, they have to be told.
Which funds or other entities does this cash reconciliation work cover, and does the same process apply across them?

I cannot give you a list of funds. The bank and account list for this has never been confirmed, so the process owner would have to tell you exactly which funds and entities are in scope. The basic method is the same everywhere: every cash movement gets categorized and the categories have to equal the bank balance. What changes from client to client is the rules around it. Working-capital rules, LPA timing windows, line-of-credit obligations, sweep-account arrangements, affiliate structures and even the workbook design all vary, so we record and apply each client's current approved method and we do not make up a standard formula. That is where it goes wrong. If an LPA or line-of-credit term changes when cash is actually available, we have to apply the governing term through FA-19 or the approved client methodology, and we only proceed once the client or an authorized reviewer has confirmed the treatment and it is documented against the governing documents. People quote 30 to 90 days for when a distribution can happen under an LPA, but that is only typical, the fund's own LPA controls. The other one is affiliates. If an affiliate balance is missing the entity, the transaction or the expected repayment, it goes to the fund team or the client and it is not treated as available cash until the details and treatment are approved.
What decisions or actions does the cash reconciliation and working-capital report support?

It is there so people can decide on capital calls, distributions, fees, line-of-credit activity and other liquidity needs, and it feeds the payment funding check in FA-17 as well as quarterly reporting and liquidity conversations with the client. The fund or capital-activity team takes it to the decision-makers and tells them the available cash, what is set aside for a purpose, the pending obligations and the projected ending balance, and says whether a capital call, a hold or some other action is needed. Who is actually allowed to recommend and approve that action has not been confirmed, so I cannot tell you. Two things go wrong here. First, if pending outflows are more than the available cash, I flag the shortfall in the event liquidity view and it goes for a capital-event or payment decision by the client or the fund team, and nothing proceeds until that action is complete and the supporting record is there. That can delay a payment or a distribution. Second, people ask me for a working-capital number. There is no approved formula, forecast period or probability threshold for it, so the working-capital calculation is on hold. If someone asks for a result I stop and escalate, because an unapproved model cannot be used to approve or fund an amount. The examples in the training deck people call the Beta deck are not policy.
How do you determine which cash is set aside for a particular purpose in the liquidity view?

It comes from the categories. In the Cash Composition tab every movement sits in a life-to-date source or use category. Sources are things like capital calls, line-of-credit draws and proceeds, and uses are investments, management fees, expenses, line-of-credit repayments and distributions, with amounts due to or from affiliates kept as their own category. Each categorized amount stays linked to its transaction in the detailed list, so I can show where the cash on hand came from and what it is meant for. On top of that there is a forward-liquidity section where I record expected outflows that are not in the bank or the GL yet, from client advance notices or approved internal commitments, with the amount, timing, purpose and account, and I keep those separate from cash already recorded in the GL. When the cash actually moves I update or close the item. The rule is that I do not treat the bank cash at a point in time as fully available when known obligations are pending. Where it goes wrong is the notices. They come in as separate, uncoordinated emails and one can get missed, and a missing expected item overstates available cash, so I log each approved one rather than relying on the email. There is also no confirmed rule for closing out stale expected items and no standard set of fields for them, so I cannot tell you when an old one should come off. The process owner would need to confirm that. Before an event the decision team reviews that the known outflows are shown separately from available cash.
Roughly how many cash movements do you usually categorize in a month?

I do not have a count I would stand behind. Nobody has measured it, so I would rather not guess, and the process owner would be the person to ask. What I can tell you is that the volume is not the hard part, the detail is. Each movement is one row, and the descriptions carry so little detail that some of the context lives in people's heads. So I am not supposed to rely on a label like Cap Call number 12 received, I add whatever event, investor and transaction detail is available. Capital-event months are where the mistakes happen. If an event is net overall, I have to show the full contribution as a cash inflow and the full distribution as a cash outflow, not just the net amount. Early or late investor receipts go in the Due To/From category with the event reference. I match the investor receipt totals to the Cash Composition amount using the portal and bank details, and when they do not match, the detailed receivable exceptions and any unidentified investor wires go over to FA-02.
What does FA-02 do with the detailed receivable exceptions and unidentified investor wires it receives?
This capture still has open sections. 14 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

notes.summary: The participant does not have a measured monthly movement count. They describe gross recording for net capital events, treatment of early or late receipts, and a receipt-total check that can send exceptions to FA-02.

draft.title: Current-practice draft: Cash Reconciliation & Working Capital Reporting
draft.overview: Draft for process-owner review, based on one participant’s account. It describes cash categorization and reconciliation, event liquidity information, quarterly review and the hold on the working-capital calculation. Overall ownership, scope, completion and several handoffs remain UNKNOWN. No supporting documents were supplied or reviewed.
draft.trigger: Cash activity appears in the bank portal, the monthly bank reconciliation identifies activity, or a planned capital event needs liquidity analysis.
inputs: Bank portal activity and bank records, including sweep accounts.
Monthly bank reconciliation and prior reconciled workbook.
Client advance notices and approved internal commitments.
Current approved client methods, applicable governing terms and transaction details.
Investor receipt totals and portal and bank details.
outputs: Forward-liquidity information and event shortfall flags.
Cash-position information for decision-makers, quarterly reporting and the FA-17 payment funding check.
Exceptions, variance notes and referrals where applicable.
exceptions: Beginning-balance mismatch: record and hold the item until resolved or an authorized decision is documented; the correction procedure and approver are unconfirmed.
Any failed update check: record the exception and hold the affected item until resolved or an authorized decision is documented.
Remaining category difference: escalate with a variance note; the report should not be relied on until resolved and documented.
Unclear transaction purpose: request details from the fund team or client and hold the item until resolved and supported.
Quarterly and Treasury copies differ: escalate alignment; proceed only on agreement or an approved and documented difference, and tell anyone who relied on an earlier report.
Incomplete affiliate balance: refer it and exclude it from available cash until details and treatment are approved.
Liquidity shortfall: flag it and obtain a capital-event or payment decision; nothing proceeds until the action is complete and a supporting record exists.
Working-capital calculation request: stop and escalate while the calculation is on hold.
Investor receipt mismatch: refer detailed receivable exceptions and any unidentified wires to FA-02.
controls: Beginning balance must match the prior ending and actual bank balances including sweeps.
On every update, the participant checks category-to-bank equality, category support and transaction uniqueness.
A reviewer looks at the bank-to-category match; the reconciliation records that review.
Prior-year changes require supporting records and review.
Quarterly output is tested against approved period source data, and quarterly corrections are listed.
Changed availability treatment requires client or authorized reviewer confirmation and documentation against governing documents.
Before an event, the decision team reviews that known outflows are separate from available cash.
validation_notes: This is an AI-generated current-practice draft for review. Participant confirmation and process-owner approval are pending; the capture is not complete or independently verified.
No supporting documents were supplied or reviewed. LPA terms, FA-19, FA-17, FA-02 and the Beta deck are participant-reported references, not verified source rules.
The participant reports intended daily updates and actual slippage to weekly or monthly; neither is treated as a measured performance figure.
The three update checks are reported for every update. Their relative order, concurrent execution and a joint release gateway are not established.
The reported correction and recheck routes cite the participant’s answer about checks after correction. The three checks are rerun on every update; the map does not assert their order.

The proposed S8-to-S19 edge is omitted: a reviewer looks at the bank-to-category match, but the account does not establish that a successful participant check directly hands off to that review. The review remains a known disconnected action.
The proposed S4-to-S34 edge is omitted: the account describes both updating the workbook and matching investor receipts but does not establish their direct sequence.

Carry-forward, client-method application, affiliate handling, pre-event review, presentation and other known fragments lack established placement or exits. Their disconnection does not establish separate processes.
Version-difference and other exception holds retain their reported release conditions without inventing a return after release.
The participant’s basic method is one account, not an independently corroborated or approved GPFS standard.

steps.title: Cash activity appears in portal
steps.description: Cash activity appearing in the bank portal can initiate the work.

steps.title: Monthly reconciliation finds activity
steps.description: The monthly bank reconciliation can identify activity that starts the work.

steps.title: Planned capital event
steps.description: A planned capital event needing liquidity analysis can initiate the work.

steps.title: Update cash composition workbook
steps.description: Categorize movements as life-to-date sources or uses and link each categorized amount to its detailed transaction. Sources include capital calls, credit-line draws and proceeds; uses include investments, management fees, expenses, credit-line repayments and distributions. Amounts due to or from affiliates have their own category. Each movement is one row, with available event, investor and transaction detail. For a net capital event show the full contribution as an inflow and full distribution as an outflow; put early or late investor receipts in Due To/From with the event reference.

steps.title: Carry workbook into period
steps.description: Carry the workbook into a new period.

steps.title: Does beginning balance match?
steps.description: Check the beginning balance against the prior ending balance and actual bank balance including sweeps. Trace the beginning balance to the prior reconciled workbook and bank records. The precise placement of the trace within the check is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Record and hold balance exception
steps.description: Record a beginning-balance mismatch and hold the affected item until it is resolved or an authorized decision is documented. The carry-forward correction procedure and fix approver are unconfirmed.

steps.title: Do cash categories match bank?
steps.system: Cash Composition workbook and bank records
steps.description: On every update, check that cash categories total the actual bank balance including sweeps. There is no tolerance; the commonly mentioned amount under ten dollars is not an approved rounding tolerance.

steps.title: Investigate category difference
steps.description: Look for missing transactions, duplicate entries, broken formulas or links, and misclassifications. Continue until the categorized total matches the bank balance including sweeps. Escalate any difference left with a variance note; the report should not be relied on until it is resolved and documented.

steps.title: Confirm missing movement
steps.description: Confirm the account, entity, date, amount and whether cash came in or went out against the bank record before adding a missing movement.

steps.title: Add missing movement
steps.description: Add the confirmed movement as its own row with date, description, amount and cash category. A fix changing prior-year history is made only with supporting records and review.

steps.title: Correct duplicate movement
steps.description: Ensure the movement appears only once and matches the bank record. Duplicates can arise when the same movement is picked up from the portal and monthly reconciliation. A prior-year change requires supporting records and review.

steps.title: Correct broken formulas or links
steps.description: Correct and document broken formulas or links before the workbook is used again. A prior-year change requires supporting records and review.

steps.title: Request unclear transaction details
steps.description: If a transaction cannot be assigned to a category, do not guess. Keep it as an explicit exception and ask the fund team or client for details. Stop the item until it is resolved and documented with supporting documents or correspondence. A prior-year change also requires supporting records and review.

steps.title: Escalate remaining variance
steps.description: Escalate any difference left with a variance note. Nobody should rely on the report until the difference is resolved and documented. Recipient, note location and resolution procedure are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Does each category trace to activity?
steps.description: On every update, check that every category traces to identifiable activity. Who reviews or approves this check has not been confirmed.

steps.title: Is each movement listed once?
steps.description: On every update, check that each movement appears in the transaction list only once. Who reviews or approves this check has not been confirmed.

steps.title: Record and hold failed check
steps.description: If any update check fails, record the exception and do not advance the affected item until it is resolved or an authorized decision is documented. Recording location and decision authority are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review bank-to-category match
steps.description: A reviewer looks at the bank-to-category match; the reconciliation is the record of that review. Timing and the person recording it are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Copy report to quarterly files
steps.description: Copy the report into quarterly supporting files for detailed quarterly review. The day-to-day copy in the Treasury folder receives much less review.

steps.title: Review quarterly report
steps.description: Review the quarterly copy and identified differences. The test is that quarterly output reconciles to approved source data for the period. Corrections made in the quarterly copy are listed; who lists them and where is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Do report versions agree?
steps.system: Treasury folder and quarterly supporting files
steps.description: Compare the quarterly and Treasury-folder copies. A version comparison and resolution record are kept; their owner and location are UNKNOWN. Placement relative to quarterly review is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Escalate version differences
steps.description: Identify differences and escalate the need to align the copies to the reviewer or process owner. Proceed only when versions agree or the difference is approved and documented. If someone already relied on an earlier report, they must be told. The final alignment owner and method for transferring quarterly corrections back to the operational copy are unconfirmed.

steps.title: Apply approved client method
steps.description: Record and apply each client’s current approved method rather than inventing a standard formula. When an LPA or credit-line term changes actual cash availability, apply the governing term through FA-19 or the approved client methodology. Proceed only once the client or an authorized reviewer confirms the treatment and it is documented against the governing documents. The participant describes 30–90 days as typical, not a rule; the fund’s own LPA controls.

steps.title: Refer incomplete affiliate balance
steps.description: If an affiliate balance is missing the entity, transaction or expected repayment, refer it to the fund team or client. Do not treat it as available cash until the details and treatment are approved.

steps.title: Log expected outflows
steps.description: Record expected outflows not yet in the bank or GL from client advance notices or approved internal commitments, including amount, timing, purpose and account. Keep them separate from cash already recorded in the GL and log each approved notice rather than relying on uncoordinated emails. There is no confirmed standard field set or stale-item closure rule.

steps.title: Update or close expected item
steps.description: When cash actually moves, update or close the expected item. The criteria for choosing update rather than closure are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review outflows before event
steps.description: Before an event, review that known outflows are shown separately from available cash. The participant does not treat bank cash at a point in time as fully available when known obligations are pending.

steps.title: Analyze event liquidity
steps.description: A planned capital event can require liquidity analysis. The full sequence and its relationship to logging outflows, client methods and the pre-event review are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Flag event liquidity shortfall
steps.description: If pending outflows exceed available cash, flag the shortfall in the event liquidity view.

steps.title: Make shortfall decision
steps.description: The shortfall goes for a capital-event or payment decision by the client or fund team. Nothing proceeds until the action is complete and a supporting record exists. This can delay a payment or distribution. Individual recommendation and approval authority is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Present cash position
steps.description: Take the report to decision-makers and explain available cash, amounts set aside, pending obligations and projected ending balance, including whether a capital call, hold or another action is needed. Who is authorized to recommend and approve the action is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Escalate working-capital request
steps.description: If asked for a working-capital result, stop and escalate. The calculation is on hold because no formula, forecast period or probability threshold is approved. An unapproved model cannot be used to approve or fund an amount. The participant says the Beta training deck examples are not policy.

steps.title: Refer exceptions to FA-02
steps.description: When investor receipt totals do not match Cash Composition, detailed receivable exceptions and any unidentified investor wires go to FA-02. Sender and subsequent handling are UNKNOWN.

topics.answer: The intake calls the work Cash Reconciliation & Working Capital Reporting. The participant refers to the Cash Composition workbook, Cash Analysis tab and event liquidity view. Other team or checklist names and the full boundary are UNKNOWN.

The report supports decisions on capital calls, distributions, fees, credit-line activity and other liquidity needs. It feeds FA-17’s payment funding check, quarterly reporting and client liquidity conversations. The precise delivered result and completion boundary remain UNKNOWN.

Bank portal activity, activity found in the monthly bank reconciliation, or a planned capital event needing liquidity analysis can start the work. Workbook updates are intended daily when cash moves but often slip to weekly or monthly. Who detects each trigger and any fixed deadlines are UNKNOWN.

Held items require resolution or a documented authorized decision. Categories must reconcile to bank without tolerance; quarterly versions must agree or their difference be approved and documented before proceeding. The overall finished condition, delivery evidence and closure boundary are UNKNOWN. The report is used by decision-makers, FA-17 and quarterly reporting.
UNKNOWN. The participant performs updates and checks; a reviewer and quarterly reviewer perform reviews, but overall accountability is not established.

The participant carries the workbook into a new period, checks and traces its opening balance, categorizes movements and reruns three update checks. Differences are investigated and corrected or held and escalated. Expected outflows are logged separately and updated or closed when cash moves. A quarterly copy is reviewed against approved source data, and version differences are escalated. The fund or capital-activity team presents the cash position; a shortfall goes to the client or fund team for a decision. Several placements, handoffs and returns are UNKNOWN.

The participant checks bank equality, category traceability and duplicate movements on every update; a reviewer looks at the bank match and the reconciliation records it. Detailed quarterly review tests output against approved period source data. Failed checks hold affected items; prior-year fixes require support and review. Review authority for the other two checks, evidence locations, thresholds, segregation, override authority and several failure routes are UNKNOWN.

The participant says categorization and bank equality are common, but working-capital rules, LPA timing, credit obligations, sweeps, affiliate structures and workbook design vary by client. Each client’s current approved method is recorded and applied. Exact step differences, charging, removal constraints and the basis for a general GPFS standard are UNKNOWN.

Daily updates often slip, descriptions lack detail and context can reside in people’s heads. Separate uncoordinated notice emails can be missed; operational and quarterly copies can disagree. The participant describes self-checking as a weakness and says the day-to-day copy receives less review. Quantified effort is UNKNOWN.

A missed expected outflow overstates available cash. A shortfall can delay a payment or distribution; capital-event months are where mistakes occur. An unresolved category difference makes the report unsuitable for reliance, and prior users of an earlier report must be told when applicable. Other consequences and frequency are UNKNOWN.

The participant mentions the workbook, bank records, reconciliation, quarterly supporting files, client methods, governing documents and a Beta training deck. The participant says the deck’s examples are not policy. No supporting documents were supplied or reviewed; availability and locations beyond those named are UNKNOWN.

The participant cannot list the funds or confirm the bank and account list. The basic method is said to apply everywhere, with client-specific rules and designs, but the basis for general GPFS applicability and the parent-process boundary are UNKNOWN.

The participant reports no category-to-bank tolerance, client-approved methods, governing LPA or credit terms for changed cash availability, and prior-year support and review requirements. The fund’s own LPA controls rather than the commonly quoted 30–90-day range. Changed-term treatment needs confirmation and documentation. No working-capital formula, forecast period or probability threshold is approved, so that calculation is on hold. Interpretation authority, source conflicts and detailed calculation lineage are UNKNOWN; no governing documents were reviewed.

Bank activity, monthly reconciliation, client notices and approved commitments supply inputs. The report feeds FA-17’s funding check and quarterly reporting; the fund or capital-activity team takes it to decision-makers. Investor receipt exceptions and unidentified wires go to FA-02 on mismatch. FA-19 or an approved client methodology is used for applicable governing terms. Readiness signals, downstream processing and several handoffs are UNKNOWN.

The participant works with a Cash Composition workbook, Cash Analysis and Cash Composition tabs, a forward-liquidity section, bank portal and records, and Treasury and quarterly file copies. Movements and expected outflows are entered as rows or logged; formulas and links may require correction. The authoritative record, workbook logic ownership, full storage locations and calculation lineage are UNKNOWN.

The participant would not estimate monthly movement counts because they have not been measured. Capital-event months are where mistakes occur, and transaction detail rather than volume is described as the hard part. Exception rates and effort by step are UNKNOWN.
